# driftd

<!-- badges: start -->
<!-- badges: end -->

driftd provides a streamlined workflow for fitting Drift‑Diffusion Models (DDMs) to trial‑level RT and binary response data, performing participant‑level maximum‑likelihood fits (via `nlminb`/`rtdists`) with standard errors, and checks of model fit that compare observed and predicted response probabilities and RT quantiles.

## Installation

From CRAN (when available):

```r
install.packages("driftd")
```

Development version from GitHub:

```r
devtools::install_github("JStrueder/driftd")
```

## Quick Example: Fitting, Checking, Comparing and Validating Models

This example demonstrates the typical workflow. Fitting can be slow, so the fitting step is shown with `eval = FALSE`. Use the included example dataset to follow along.

```{r example, eval = FALSE}
library(driftd)

# load example data included with the package
data(example_data)

# Quick inspect
head(example_data)

# Fit the model (this may take time; run interactively)
results <- driftd(
  data = example_data,
  sub_id = "ID",
  response = "R",
  rt = "RT",
  vary_z = c("val"),
  vary_v = c("prob", "val"),
  fix_st0 = TRUE,
  fix_sz = TRUE,
  fix_sv = TRUE,
  print_starting_vals = FALSE
)

# Examine results
results$summary                              # mean and SD of each parameter
est <- estimates(results)                    # one row per participant and parameter, with SEs
cells <- estimates(results, format = "cells")  # one row per participant and condition cell

# e.g. a repeated-measures ANOVA on the drift rates
cells$ID <- factor(cells$ID)
cells$prob <- factor(cells$prob)
summary(aov(v ~ prob * val + Error(ID / (prob * val)), data = cells))

# Model fit: observed vs predicted response probabilities and RT quantiles,
# with prediction intervals from 200 simulated datasets
pred <- predict(results, seed = 1)

pred                   # one row per participant, condition, response and statistic
aggregate(pred)        # group averages per condition cell
summary(pred)          # misfit per participant, worst first

plot(pred)                                   # RT quantiles: panels by prob, colors by val
plot(pred, type = "choice")                  # response probabilities
plot(pred, response_labels = c(upper = "pos choice", lower = "neg choice"))
plot(pred, type = "scatter")                 # observed vs predicted, all statistics
plot(pred, type = "participants")            # participants with poor fit
plot(pred, participant = 3)                  # a single participant

# Model comparison: e.g. does val also affect the starting point?
results_v <- driftd(data = example_data, sub_id = "ID", response = "R", rt = "RT",
                    vary_v = c("prob", "val"))
cmp <- compare_models(drift_only = results_v, drift_and_bias = results)
cmp                    # summed AIC/BIC, participants per best model, likelihood-ratio test
plot(cmp)              # BIC differences per participant

# Parameter recovery: can the parameters be recovered with this design and trial count?
rec <- recover_parameters(results, seed = 1)
rec                    # correlation, bias and RMSE of true vs recovered values
plot(rec)

# Model recovery: can the compared models be told apart? (slow: fits every model to data
# simulated from every model)
mrec <- recover_models(drift_only = results_v, drift_and_bias = results, seed = 1)
mrec                   # confusion matrix: generating vs selected model
plot(mrec)

# Simulate replicate datasets from the fitted model
sims <- simulate(results, nsim = 10, seed = 1)
```
